# windows_service (Resource)

Manages the full lifecycle of a Windows service on a remote host via SSH and PowerShell. Supports create, update, in-place reconfiguration, runtime state control (Running/Stopped/Paused), deletion and import.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: a service running as LocalSystem.
resource "windows_service" "example" {
  name         = "example-svc"
  display_name = "Example Service"
  description  = "Managed by Terraform."
  binary_path  = "C:\\Program Files\\Example\\example.exe --run"
  start_type   = "Automatic"
  status       = "Running"
}

# Slow or heavily loaded host: bound every remote operation explicitly.
# Without this block each operation defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled
# PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of
# blocking Terraform indefinitely.
resource "windows_service" "slow_host" {
  name         = "slow-svc"
  display_name = "Slow Host Service"
  binary_path  = "C:\\Program Files\\Example\\example.exe --run"
  start_type   = "Automatic"
  status       = "Running"

  timeouts = {
    create = "20m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "20m"
    delete = "20m"
  }
}

# Write-only credential rotation (issue #194): the plaintext never reaches
# `terraform.tfstate`. Rotation is driven exclusively by
# `service_password_wo_version` — change it and re-apply with the new password
# value; changing only `service_password_wo` without changing the version is
# a no-op.
resource "windows_service" "app_wo" {
  name                        = "myapp-wo"
  display_name                = "My Application (WriteOnly)"
  description                 = "Business application managed by Terraform."
  binary_path                 = "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp\\myapp.exe"
  start_type                  = "Automatic"
  status                      = "Running"
  service_account             = "DOMAIN\\svc-myapp"
  service_password_wo         = var.svc_myapp_password
  service_password_wo_version = 1
  dependencies                = ["LanmanServer", "Tcpip"]
}

# Advanced example: service running under a domain account with dependencies.
resource "windows_service" "app" {
  name             = "myapp"
  display_name     = "My Application"
  description      = "Business application managed by Terraform."
  binary_path      = "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp\\myapp.exe"
  start_type       = "AutomaticDelayedStart"
  status           = "Running"
  service_account  = "DOMAIN\\svc-myapp"
  service_password = var.svc_myapp_password
  dependencies     = ["LanmanServer", "Tcpip"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `binary_path` (String) Full path to the service executable including any arguments. ForceNew.
- `name` (String) Short name of the Windows service. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).

### Optional

- `dependencies` (List of String) Ordered list of short service names this service depends on.
- `description` (String) Textual description of the service.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable display name shown in services.msc. Defaults to name if omitted.
- `service_account` (String) Account under which the service runs. Defaults to LocalSystem.
- `service_password` (String, Sensitive, Deprecated) **Deprecated, use `service_password_wo`.** Password for `service_account`. Sensitive and semantic write-only on the Windows side (not read back), but **persisted as a Sensitive value in `terraform.tfstate`** under the legacy attribute. For a no-state-leak alternative see `service_password_wo`.

The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.
- `service_password_wo` (String, Sensitive) Write-only password for `service_account` (TPF v1.14+). Same Windows-side semantics as `service_password` (sent to `Set-Service` / SCM on Create / version-gated Update), **but the plaintext is never persisted in `terraform.tfstate`** — the framework drops it from state automatically.

The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.

Because the value is not in state, Terraform cannot detect changes to the password content. Rotation is driven exclusively by `service_password_wo_version`: increment the version and re-apply with the new password value. Changing only `service_password_wo` without bumping the version is a no-op.

Mutually exclusive with `service_password`.
- `service_password_wo_version` (Number) Version counter for `service_password_wo` rotation. Change this value to rotate the password: when it changes between prior state and plan, the provider re-applies the password via the SCM `Change` call regardless of whether the password value changed. Conventionally starts at 1. Changing only `service_password_wo` without changing this version leaves the stored credential untouched. Removing the version is not a rotation.
- `start_type` (String) Service start mode. One of: Automatic, AutomaticDelayedStart, Manual, Disabled.
- `status` (String) Desired runtime state: Running, Stopped, or Paused. Null = observe-only.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `current_status` (String) Observed runtime state from the last Read (Running, Stopped, Paused).
- `id` (String) Resource identifier, equal to the Windows short service name.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing service by its short Windows service name.
terraform import windows_service.example example-svc
```
